title: PvP AutoReducer can raise iPhone quality when connection degrades

environment.browser: runtime policy bug is browser-independent; mobile acceptance uses iPhone-sized Playwright
environment.surface: active online PvP -> sustained input/ack degradation -> adaptive presentation quality

reproduction: Load Kelo World on a phone-sized viewport so KELO_PERF selects its normal `performance` profile.
Enter active online PvP and sustain enough input->ack degradation for KeloPvPAutoReducer to pass its bad-hold and grace windows.
In V1, AutoReducer calls KELO_PERF.setManualQuality('medium') for the first reduction.
Observe that setManualQuality overrides the device's `performance` base and makes the effective profile `medium`, increasing visual budgets instead of reducing them.
expected: A PvP protection request must be monotonic: it may leave current quality unchanged or reduce it, but it must never improve quality when network conditions worsen. Recovery must restore the pre-existing base/manual policy.
actual: V1 requested manual `medium` first and `performance` only for emergency. On phone-sized clients already at `performance`, the first network degradation could therefore increase quality to `medium`; emergency provided no level below the phone baseline.
evidence: src/systems/performance-governor.js main@325c7fd: phone viewport selects profileIndex=3 (`performance`) and setManualQuality() overrides the base profile.
src/systems/pvp-auto-reducer.js V1: degrade() requested `medium`, then critical path requested `performance`.
PR #410 adds a 390x844 deterministic regression proving a floor above the current profile cannot upgrade it and dedicated PvP floors can move below `performance`.
owner_hint: KELO_PERF quality policy with KeloPvPAutoReducer as PvP presentation orchestrator

research.summary: The defect is a composition error between device quality and PvP adaptation. V1 used the manual-quality API, which is an override rather than a degradation floor. Because phone-sized clients already begin at `performance`, asking for `medium` on bad network conditions inverted the intended direction. The candidate adds a monotonic floor primitive to KELO_PERF and reserves lower profiles for explicit PvP use.

known_facts.statement: On viewport min dimension <=844, KELO_PERF initializes profileIndex=3, which is `performance` in V1.
V1 AutoReducer first calls setManualQuality('medium') after sustained degradation and later calls setManualQuality('performance') for critical degradation.
setManualQuality() takes precedence over the automatic device profile, so `medium` becomes effective even when the base is `performance`.

The candidate defines `pvp_low` and `pvp_emergency` below `performance`, caps generic autotuning at `performance`, and composes them through setQualityFloor() so a floor cannot improve the current base/manual profile.

The candidate freezes generic autotuning while a temporary quality floor is active, so clearing the floor restores the exact pre-floor automatic/manual policy instead of a hidden quality change accumulated during reduced load.

hypotheses.theory: Using the manual-quality override for a relative degradation policy causes the quality direction inversion on phones.
hypotheses.why: The V1 control flow deterministically maps a performance-base phone to manual medium after sustained bad network conditions; no runtime timing assumption is needed beyond entering the documented degrade path.
hypotheses.test_next: Run the permanent 390x844 quality-floor audit and the repository mobile/PvP gates on the exact PR bytes.

ruled_out.theory: The fix requires direct canvas/back-buffer manipulation from AutoReducer.
ruled_out.reason: The root bug is policy composition, and ENGINE_MAP forbids new features from writing canvas/camera/zoom directly. The owner-native quality floor corrects the inversion without a parallel render controller.

unknowns.question: How much real-device frame-time improvement each new PvP floor produces under a congested match on physical iPhone Safari.
unknowns.why_it_matters: The bug fix proves monotonic behavior; tuning the exact particle/animation budgets is a separate measured optimization question.
unknowns.quickest_test: Capture KELO_PERF frame telemetry and AutoReducer snapshot during an intentionally stressed physical-iPhone PvP session.

external_references.title: MDN WebGL best practices — smaller back buffer
external_references.lesson: Lower presentation quality can trade visual fidelity for speed, but Kelo's current owner rules mean any future backing-buffer adaptation must live behind the proper render/performance owner rather than inside the PvP feature.

attempt_history.goal: Make PvP adaptive quality strictly monotonic and preserve the device/player quality policy on recovery.

change.summary: Added owner-native temporary quality floors, dedicated PvP low/emergency profiles, an autotune cap at normal performance, kill switch, silent protection during notice cooldown, and a deterministic 390x844 regression.

validation.method: Permanent quality-floor audit plus Performance, PvP first-use and Main Stability mobile gates on exact PR bytes.
evidence: GitHub Actions checks are attached to PR #410 and were still running when the candidate record was created.

attempt_history.conclusion: Candidate implementation is complete enough for independent CI verification; no success claim is made before the gates finish.
attempt_history.do_not_repeat_without: If the permanent monotonicity audit passes but real-device telemetry shows insufficient benefit, tune only presentation budgets with measured before/after evidence; do not reintroduce manual-quality overrides.

next_best_actions.action: Complete PR #410 Main Stability, PvP First-Use and pvp-auto-reducer audits on the exact candidate bytes.
next_best_actions.reason: These gates independently test the new monotonic policy, lazy PvP integration and mandatory 390x844 sustained-walk freeze firewall.
next_best_actions.expected_signal: Quality audit proves performance cannot be raised to medium, PvP first-use stays functional, and mobile sustained walking remains responsive.
next_best_actions.stop_condition: If any gate fails, keep BUG-0005 FIXED_PENDING_VERIFY, record the failure and repair the candidate before merge.

next_best_actions.action: Measure real-device PvP frame telemetry under intentionally stressed connection/render conditions.
next_best_actions.reason: This tunes the strength of pvp_low/pvp_emergency after correctness is proven.
next_best_actions.expected_signal: Reduced particle/distant-animation work lowers frame pressure without harming combat readability.
next_best_actions.stop_condition: Treat this as tuning rather than reopening the correctness bug unless quality direction/restoration is wrong.

fix.summary: PR #410 replaces manual quality overrides with a monotonic temporary floor, adds two PvP-only profiles below normal phone performance, and freezes the underlying autotuner while the floor is active so recovery restores the exact prior quality policy.

verification.method: Independent GitHub Actions on PR #410; permanent regression is `npm run audit:pvp-auto-reducer` plus mobile/PvP stability gates.

notes: This bug was discovered while continuing the requested PvP AutoReducer implementation; it is separate from the PvP first-use lifecycle defect in BUG-0004.
The candidate deliberately does not mutate canvas/camera/zoom from KeloPvPAutoReducer because ENGINE_MAP assigns those responsibilities elsewhere.
